subject: Polity
topic: Union Executive — Vice President and PM
sub_topic: Election and role of Vice President

concepts.name: Electoral College for Vice President: Composition and Uniqueness
key_dimensions: Both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha) vote — NOT state legislatures, unlike President
Nominated members of Parliament ARE included (trap: they are excluded from Presidential election)
Elected members only vs. all members — distinction from Presidential electoral college
Why state assemblies are excluded: VP is not a constitutional head of states

concepts.name: Method of Election: Single Transferable Vote via Proportional Representation
key_dimensions: Secret ballot system under Article 66
Preference voting mechanism — how votes are transferred and quota calculated
Distinction from First-Past-The-Post used in general elections
Similarity with Presidential election method but difference in electoral college size and composition

concepts.name: Constitutional Provisions Governing VP Election: Article 66
key_dimensions: Article 66(1): Electoral college composition
Article 66(3): Qualifications — must be citizen, 35 years, qualified to be Rajya Sabha member
Article 66(4): VP shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or any state legislature
If a sitting member is elected VP, their seat becomes vacant — automatic vacation rule

concepts.name: Qualifications for Vice President: Constitutional Requirements and Disqualifications
key_dimensions: Must be a citizen of India, age 35+, qualified to be a member of Rajya Sabha
Must NOT hold any office of profit under Union, State, or local authority (exception: President, VP, Governor, Minister)
Distinction: VP qualification tied to Rajya Sabha membership, President's to Lok Sabha membership — common UPSC trap
Cannot be a member of either House of Parliament or state legislature at time of election

concepts.name: Term of Office and Conditions of Service of Vice President
key_dimensions: Fixed term of 5 years under Article 67 — but can resign, be removed, or continue till successor enters
Resignation addressed to the President (trap: President resigns to VP)
Eligible for re-election — no bar on number of terms (contrast with no explicit bar on President too)
Salary and allowances charged to Consolidated Fund of India

concepts.name: Removal of Vice President: Process and Constitutional Safeguards
key_dimensions: Article 67(b): Removed by resolution of Rajya Sabha passed by effective majority + agreed to by Lok Sabha (simple majority)
No impeachment process unlike President — simpler removal mechanism
14 days advance notice required before moving removal resolution
Trap: Only Rajya Sabha can initiate removal, Lok Sabha only agrees — asymmetric process

concepts.name: Vice President as Ex-Officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha: Role and Powers
key_dimensions: Article 64 makes VP the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha — presides over its sittings
Powers of Chairman: maintain order, casting vote in case of tie, certify money bills (NO — this is Speaker's power; trap)
VP as Chairman does NOT vote in Rajya Sabha proceedings except casting vote
Distinction from Speaker of Lok Sabha — Speaker is elected from among members, VP is externally elected

concepts.name: Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha vs. Vice President: Powers During Absence
key_dimensions: Deputy Chairman presides when VP is absent — elected by Rajya Sabha members from among themselves
When VP acts as President, Deputy Chairman performs VP's duties as Rajya Sabha Chairman
Deputy Chairman is removable by Rajya Sabha majority — different from VP removal process
Chain of succession: VP → Deputy Chairman → person appointed by President to preside over RS

concepts.name: Vice President Acting as President: Conditions and Duration
key_dimensions: Article 65: VP acts as President during vacancy (death, resignation, removal, inability) — not merely temporary absence
During vacancy: VP acts until new President is elected (maximum 6 months for election to be held)
During temporary absence/illness: VP discharges President's functions till President resumes
While acting as President: VP does NOT perform duties of Rajya Sabha Chairman — Deputy Chairman takes over

concepts.name: Salary and Privileges of Vice President: As VP vs. As Acting President
key_dimensions: Regular VP salary is for role as Chairman of Rajya Sabha (not a separate VP salary — important distinction)
When acting as President, VP receives President's salary and perks, not Chairman's salary
Charged to Consolidated Fund of India — not subject to Parliamentary vote
Post-retirement benefits: pension, residence — governed by VP (Emoluments) Act

concepts.name: Oath of Office of Vice President: Who Administers and Content
key_dimensions: Oath administered by the President of India (Article 69)
Oath to bear true faith and allegiance to Constitution — does NOT include oath to preserve, protect and defend Constitution (that is President's oath — trap)
Oath to faithfully discharge duties — content comparison with President's oath is a frequent MCQ area
Third Schedule of the Constitution contains the form of oath

concepts.name: Comparison: Electoral College of President vs. Vice President
key_dimensions: President: elected MPs (both houses) + elected MLAs of states + elected MLAs of Delhi & Puducherry
VP: ALL members of Parliament (elected + nominated) — NO state legislatures
Nominated MPs excluded from Presidential election but INCLUDED in VP election — the key trap
Proportional representation with single transferable vote is common to both

concepts.name: Disputes Relating to VP Election: Jurisdiction and Finality
key_dimensions: Article 71: Disputes regarding VP election decided by Supreme Court — original jurisdiction
SC decision is final and binding
Acts done by VP before SC declaration of election void are NOT invalidated — doctrine of de facto holder
Election cannot be challenged on ground of vacancies in electoral college

concepts.name: Office of Profit Restriction and Exceptions for Vice President
key_dimensions: VP cannot hold any office of profit — but President, VP, Governor, and Union/State Ministers are exempt
Sitting MP elected as VP must vacate their Parliamentary seat immediately
Sitting state legislature member elected as VP must also vacate — covers both Parliament and state
Contrast with President: same restriction but President is also exempt from office of profit bar

concepts.name: Role of Election Commission in VP Election
key_dimensions: Election Commission of India superintends, directs, and controls VP election under Article 324
Returning Officer appointed for the election — typically Secretary General of Rajya Sabha or Lok Sabha
Nomination process: candidate must be proposed by 20 electors and seconded by 20 electors
Security deposit requirement — forfeited if candidate fails to secure 1/6th of valid votes

concepts.name: Vice President's Position in the Constitutional Hierarchy and Protocol
key_dimensions: Second highest constitutional office in India in terms of warrant of precedence
VP ranks above PM in warrant of precedence — frequent confusion in MCQs
VP has no executive powers in normal circumstances — purely legislative presiding role
Distinction from US VP who is more politically active in executive branch

concepts.name: Historical and Practical Instances of VP Acting as President
key_dimensions: V.V. Giri resigned as VP to contest Presidential election — Deputy Chairman took over RS
B.D. Jatti acted as President after death of Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed in 1977
These instances illustrate constitutional machinery working in chain-of-succession scenarios
Institutional continuity principle: no vacuum in constitutional offices

concepts.name: Casting Vote Powers of VP as Rajya Sabha Chairman
key_dimensions: VP (as Chairman) does not vote in the first instance — only casts tie-breaking vote
Convention: casting vote should be used to maintain status quo or allow further debate
Contrast with Speaker of Lok Sabha who also only has casting vote — both have identical rule here
Trap: VP does not have a regular vote in Rajya Sabha proceedings despite being Chairman

concepts.name: Nominated Members' Voting Rights in VP Election: Constitutional Anomaly
key_dimensions: Article 66 explicitly includes nominated members of both Houses in VP electoral college
Rationale: VP is head of Rajya Sabha which includes nominated members — their inclusion is logical
Contrast: nominated members excluded from Presidential election as they don't represent popular will
This distinction is one of the most frequently tested traps in UPSC Prelims

concepts.name: Vacancy in VP Office: Causes and Constitutional Consequences
key_dimensions: Vacancy arises due to: expiry of term, death, resignation (to President), removal, or otherwise
No specific time limit mentioned in Constitution for filling VP vacancy (unlike President's 6-month rule for vacancy)
During VP vacancy, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides — no acting VP designation exists
Contrast with Presidential vacancy where VP automatically becomes acting President
